newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mbeki to talk peace with Zaire's Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mbeki to talk peace with Zaire's Mobutu.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki jets into Kinshasa on Sunday to meet Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko over efforts to obtain a ceasefire and peace talks, his spokesman said on Saturday.
"I can confirm the deputy president's leaving for Kinshasa tomorrow (Sunday) where he's going to be meeting with President Mobutu," Mbeki's spokesman Ricky Naidoo told Reuters.
Mbeki attended a summit of African leaders in Nairobi, Kenya on Wednesday that called for an immediate ceasefire in Africa's third largest country.
Naidoo said the meeting with Mobutu would be a follow-on to those discussions ahead of a further summit in Lome, Togo, on March 26.

"It's an extension of that process. Because of the concerns applying to Zaire, the deputy president is going to consult with President Mobutu and will be briefing him on what's going on to try to arrive at a solution," Naidoo said.

He said it was not a attempt by South Africa's heir-apparent to President Nelson Mandela to digress from other international initiatives to broker a peaceful resolution to the rebellion -- launched in eastern Zaire by Laurent Kabila.

"The South African process is not an isolated process. It is part of the whole Organisation of African Unity process and that of the four heads of state also involved which includes Kenya, Zimbabwe and the Congo," Naidoo said.
Mobutu returned home to Kinshasa on Friday from a mansion on the French Riviera where he had been convalescing after prostate cancer surgery last year.
Meanwhile, Mbeki told South African state radio on Saturday that he was hopeful that both Mobutu and Kabila would attend the Lome summit.

"There must be a negotiated resolution of this question and therefore that means the government of Zaire and Kabila and his people have a need to get together. Now that might very well be the occasion when they do," the deputy president said.
